[Pull request #499](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/pull/499) landed this way.

- The coordinator may do five things in the maintainer's place, and nothing else: read a policy notice on a file whose change it has read, dismiss an equivalent mutant, dismiss a finding that restates a ruling, dismiss a refuted injection flag on Melian's own prompt text, and post the override status of the outage procedure under four conditions. [The decision](docs/decisions/2026-11-28-what-the-coordinator-may-do-for-the-maintainer.md) sets out each, and its limits. A lens's acknowledge or blocking finding stays the maintainer's.

explanation.whyHere: A later pull request that widens the delegation, for example "the coordinator may dismiss a lens's acknowledge finding" or "may read any policy notice", draws only that acknowledge notice on AGENTS.md. The coordinator can clear it, and the builder can queue. So the agents can amend their own authority without the maintainer ever reading it. The decision files under `docs/decisions/` draw no notice at all.

The `melian round` workflow reviews it. The only finding above advisory is the acknowledge policy notice on AGENTS.md, so `melian/review` is `success`. The coordinator reads the diff and posts "Coordinator: read of a policy notice". Under line 259, the builder treats that as the maintainer's read and queues. The pull request merges, and the agents now hold a wider authority that no person approved.

Choice: `melian/review` is the only required context in a second ruleset with no bypass actors. When Melian cannot run, the maintainer posts a `melian/review` `success` on the chosen pull request's head. The merge-group job copies it to the group commit, and the pull request lands through the queue. The ruleset stays `active`. If the merge-group workflow itself cannot run, the maintainer posts the same override on the entry's group commit as well. Nothing disables the ruleset.

The merge-group job accepts this as it accepts any writer's status: the creator has write permission, `target_url` names the pull request, and the reviewed base in the suffix is an ancestor of the group's base. It copies the status to the group commit. CI, thread resolution and the queue stay enforced. The override covers the commit it names, and every pull request or group that reaches that commit. The status is recorded under the maintainer's name on the head, and the job's copy on the group commit names the pull request.

explanation.whatToDo: Leave blocking policy notices, and any override of a round that reviewed the head and failed, with the maintainer. At the least, take every file in `policy-change-review`'s blocking class out of delegations 1 and 5 (`.github/**`, every `melian.yaml`, `.melian/lenses/**`, analyser configuration), and limit delegation 5 to what the outage procedure covers: Melian could not run.
explanation.whyHere: Before this change, a blocking policy notice could be cleared only by the maintainer, through a host dismissal or an override that the outage procedure limits to the case where Melian cannot run. Now the agent lanes can approve, without a person, a pull request that rewrites its own judge. That covers the round and merge-group workflows, lens prompts, `resolution`, the lens paths, `biome.json` and `tsconfig`. The only condition is the agent's own claim that it read the file, which nothing checks. The override also turns an outage tool into a way past a verdict that Melian actually reached.

properties.failureScenario: A builder's pull request edits `.github/workflows/melian-merge-group.yml` so that it copies any `melian/review` status without checking its creator. Or it edits `melian.yaml` to drop `.github/**` from `policy-change-review.files`, or to map a lens rule to `silent`. The `melian round` workflow reviews the head. The lenses report nothing above advisory, which is plausible because a lens reads YAML or workflow logic shallowly, and the guardrail raises a blocking policy notice on that file. `melian/review` is therefore `failure`. CI is green. The coordinator reads the diff, records that it read it, and posts `state=success context=melian/review description="Coordinator: override …; base <sha>"` under the maintainer's login. The merge-group job accepts it as a writer's status, and the pull request lands. No person read a change that alters how every later pull request is judged, and from then on the weakened workflow or configuration judges every head.

# What the coordinator may do for the maintainer

Status: ruled by the maintainer on 2026-11-28, in the coordinator's session. The coordinator listed the delegations below, which the maintainer had given one at a time since 2026-10-17, and asked whether to write them into the repository. He answered "yes".

Amends: [When Melian cannot run, the maintainer overrides one commit](2026-10-23-melian-review-outage-procedure.md), who may post the override on a pull request's head: the coordinator too, under the four conditions below

## Problem

The maintainer delegated some of his reads and dismissals to the coordinator, in the coordinator's session. Nothing in the repository said so. A builder cannot check a delegation it cannot read, and all three post under the maintainer's login.

Example: on [pull request #662](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/pull/662), the round's only finding above advisory was a policy notice on one new learning in AGENTS.md. The coordinator read the change and recorded its read. The builder declined to queue on it, rightly, and the pull request waited for the maintainer to answer "read".

## Choice

The coordinator may do these, and nothing else, in the maintainer's place:

1. **Read a policy notice.** The coordinator may read a `policy-change-review` notice on a file whose change it has read, and record that read on the pull request. A builder may queue on that record as it would on the maintainer's.
2. **Dismiss an equivalent mutant**, with a one-line reason that says why no input can tell the mutant from the code.
3. **Dismiss a finding that restates a ruling**: one whose only objection is to a rule the maintainer has ruled on. The dismissal names the ruling's date and where it was given.
4. **Dismiss a refuted injection flag on Melian's own prompt text**: a `melian/injection-attempt` finding the verifier refuted, where the flagged text is Melian's own prompt or its instructions for reviewers, and the coordinator has read the diff of that text and its meaning is unchang [cut at 2 KiB]
